text: The coaction extends multiplicatively from M to its exterior algebra. The square-zero relations defining that algebra in [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM) survive tensoring because the coefficient algebra H is commutative: cross terms cancel. Thus the construction respects the quotient relations, including in characteristic two; it never divides by two. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraCoact_ι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L82), [rTensor_mul_self_eq_zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/TensorProduct/SquareZero.lean#L58).
Generator coaction formula.
Square-zero relations survive tensor extension with commutative coefficients.

On a generator ι(m), the extended coaction applies the original coaction and then includes each module component into the exterior algebra. This is the defining generator rule for the quotient construction of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM). The tensor notation changes the left factor only; it does not multiply or reorder the coalgebra coefficients. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraι_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L185), [exteriorAlgebraMap_comp_exteriorAlgebraι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L238).
Generator inclusion evaluates to the ordinary exterior inclusion.
Generator rule is natural in comodule morphisms.

The extended coaction satisfies the usual right-comodule coassociativity equation of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95): coacting twice agrees with applying the coproduct to the coefficient. Both sides are algebra maps, so checking the equation on generators suffices. The associator changes tensor parentheses, while the order of the two coefficient factors stays fixed. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebra_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L163), [baseChange_subtype_endOfPoint_ιMulti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L163).
The selected structure uses the stated algebra coaction.
The resulting action on every pure wedge acts on each generator.

Applying the counit to the coefficient of the exterior coaction returns x⊗1. After the tensor-unit identification this is exactly the counitality equation in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). It holds on generators by the original comodule law and hence on the entire algebra; the displayed flipped tensor map is simply x↦x⊗1. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebra_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L163), [endOfPoint_exteriorAlgebra_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L331).
The selected comodule uses this coaction.
The induced algebra action fixes its unit.

This equips the exterior algebra with the multiplicative right coaction induced from M. The coproduct and counit equations are proved on generators, implementing the exterior representation used in [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106). The structure is explicitly selected because the same module may carry different coactions; neither finite generation nor an antipode is assumed. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraCoact_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L115), [exteriorAlgebraCoact_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L127).
Coassociativity of the algebra coaction.
Counitality of the algebra coaction.

The ordinary inclusion of M as degree-one exterior generators is packaged as a comodule morphism. Its compatibility is exactly the defining generator formula for the multiplicative coaction, in the exterior construction of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM). No basis or finite-dimensionality is needed, and the map takes a vector to a generator, not to a scalar. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraι_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L185), [exteriorAlgebraCoact_ι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L82).
The morphism evaluates to the ordinary generator inclusion.
The generator inclusion intertwines coactions.

Forgetting the compatibility proof leaves exactly the canonical linear inclusion ι:M→Λ(M). Thus the bundled morphism uses the familiar degree-one generator map of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM), with no change to its underlying function. The comodule structure is on the whole exterior algebra, while this map selects its degree-one generators. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraι_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L185), [exteriorAlgebraMap_comp_exteriorAlgebraι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L238).
Elementwise generator inclusion.
Naturality of this inclusion.

A comodule morphism f induces the usual exterior map, sending each generator ι(m) to ι(f(m)) and extending multiplicatively. This respects the relations of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM); equivariance follows by checking generators. The result is bundled as a comodule morphism, although its underlying map also preserves the algebra product and unit. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L226), [exteriorAlgebraMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L232).
Exterior maps preserve identity morphisms.
Exterior maps preserve composition.

The induced comodule morphism has exactly the linear map underlying the ordinary exterior-algebra map Λ(f). This identifies the construction with the functorial quotient of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM): every wedge factor is sent through f. Forgetting algebra multiplication in the displayed type does not change that function or its multiplicative behavior. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraMap_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L221), [exteriorAlgebraMap_comp_exteriorAlgebraι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L238).
Elementwise equality with the ordinary exterior map.
The induced map sends generators through f.

Evaluation of the bundled exterior morphism agrees with the usual exterior-algebra map on every element, not merely pure wedges. By linearity and multiplication, its generator rule determines the action on sums of wedges as in [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM). The extra coaction-compatibility proof contributes no additional operation on elements. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L232), [exteriorAlgebraMap_comp_exteriorAlgebraι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L238).
Compatibility with composition.
Compatibility with the generator inclusion.

The coaction preserves exterior degree: an element of Λⁿ(M) maps into the image of Λⁿ(M)⊗H. The proof uses degree-one generators and multiplication, matching the grading in [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM). Here decomposeTensor denotes that image submodule; the coefficient algebra is placed in degree zero, so coefficient factors do not contribute to n. Checks pass: [exteriorPowerSubcomodule_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L281), [subtype_rTensor_exteriorPowerCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L62).
The stable subcomodule has precisely the homogeneous underlying submodule.
The restricted coaction includes back to the full exterior coaction.

An A-valued point evaluates the coefficient of the exterior coaction and thereby gives an A-algebra endomorphism of A⊗Λ(M). This realizes the action underlying [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106), now over arbitrary commutative value algebras. Only a bialgebra is assumed, so the declaration supplies an endomorphism; invertibility would require additional group structure. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_exteriorAlgebra_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L331), [endOfPoint_exteriorAlgebra_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L336).
Point evaluation fixes the unit.
Point evaluation preserves multiplication.

The algebra endomorphism obtained by evaluating an A-valued point has the same underlying linear map as the general comodule point action. It therefore matches the coefficient-evaluation dictionary in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The comparison also accounts for the tensor flip: scalar extension is written A⊗Λ(M), whereas a right coaction has its coefficient on the right. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebraEndOfPoint_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L326), [baseChange_subtype_endOfPoint_ιMulti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L163).
Elementwise agreement of the algebra and linear actions.
Agreement on homogeneous pure wedges in every degree.

Both point-action constructions return the same element of A⊗Λ(M): the algebra-map construction and the general linear action of a comodule. This is the explicit coefficient evaluation of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with the scalar factor placed first. The equality holds for arbitrary tensors and commutative A, including algebras with nilpotents. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_exteriorAlgebra_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L331), [endOfPoint_exteriorAlgebra_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L336).
The shared action fixes one.
The shared action preserves products.

The coaction on Λⁿ(M) is the unique lift of the full exterior coaction through the homogeneous inclusion tensored with H. Degree preservation gives existence; the grading splits the inclusion, giving injectivity after tensoring. This constructs the exterior action used in [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106) without assuming H flat or M free. Checks pass: [subtype_rTensor_exteriorPowerCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L62), [baseChange_subtype_endOfPoint_ιMulti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L163).
The lifted coaction includes to the full exterior coaction.
The induced point action has the ordinary wedge formula.

Including the restricted coaction of a homogeneous element recovers its coaction in the full exterior algebra. This is the defining compatibility of the exterior representation used in [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106). The tensor inclusion is injective because the homogeneous summand is split, so this formula uniquely determines the restricted coaction without a flatness assumption. Checks pass: [exteriorPower_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L81), [baseChange_subtype_endOfPoint_ιMulti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L163).
The selected exterior-power structure uses the restricted map.
Compatibility yields the pointwise wedge formula.

The homogeneous piece Λⁿ(M) becomes a right comodule by restricting the exterior-algebra coaction. Its split inclusion remains injective after tensoring with H⊗H, allowing both comodule laws to descend. This supplies the exterior representation of [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106) in arbitrary degree, including zero, without finite-generation, freeness or flatness assumptions. Checks pass: [exteriorPower_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L81), [baseChange_subtype_endOfPoint_ιMulti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L163).
The structure uses exactly the homogeneous restriction.
Point action on wedges, including the empty product in degree zero.

The explicitly selected comodule on Λⁿ(M) has precisely the restricted coaction constructed above. This identifies the abstract structure with the homogeneous exterior action used in [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106). Mathlib realizes Λⁿ(M) as a submodule of the exterior algebra; the equation changes neither its carrier nor the restriction map. Checks pass: [subtype_rTensor_exteriorPowerCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L62), [baseChange_subtype_endOfPoint_ιMulti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L163).
The stated coaction agrees with the ambient one after inclusion.
The associated point action agrees with applying the point to each wedge factor.

The ordinary inclusion of Λⁿ(M) into Λ(M) is a comodule morphism because the homogeneous coaction was constructed to intertwine this inclusion. It realizes the graded inclusion for the exterior action of [Milne, Lemma 4.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=106). The map preserves the given degree and requires no choice of basis or flatness of the coefficient algebra. Checks pass: [exteriorPowerSubtype_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L103), [exteriorPowerSubtype_comp_exteriorPowerMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L147).
Evaluation is the ordinary homogeneous inclusion.
The inclusion is natural under induced exterior maps.

Forgetting coaction compatibility from the homogeneous inclusion returns the ordinary submodule inclusion Λⁿ(M)→Λ(M). Thus the bundled map is exactly the graded inclusion of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM), not a projection onto that degree. Its injectivity comes from the subtype, and the grading additionally makes its tensor extensions injective. Checks pass: [exteriorPowerSubtype_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L103), [exteriorPowerSubtype_comp_exteriorPowerMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L147).
The underlying function is the subtype inclusion.
Compatibility with exterior functoriality.

A comodule morphism f induces Λⁿ(f), acting on a pure wedge by applying f to every factor, as in the exterior construction of [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM). Compatibility with the coactions follows after the injective homogeneous tensor inclusion from compatibility of Λ(f). No invertibility or injectivity of f is required. Checks pass: [exteriorPowerMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L135), [exteriorPowerMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L140).
Exterior-power maps preserve identities.
Exterior-power maps preserve composition.

The bundled map on exterior powers has the ordinary linear map Λⁿ(f) as its underlying map. This matches the degree-n functor arising from the exterior quotient in [Stacks, §10.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DM). The coaction proof adds equivariance without changing the action on wedges; n is any natural number, including zero. Checks pass: [exteriorPowerMap_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L130), [exteriorPowerSubtype_comp_exteriorPowerMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L147).
Elementwise agreement with the ordinary exterior-power map.
Agreement with the full exterior map through homogeneous inclusions.

Changing coefficients along a bialgebra morphism f:H→K commutes with forming the multiplicative exterior coaction: apply f to the coefficient after coacting. Checking generators proves the equality. Under the right-comodule dictionary of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), this is restriction of representations along the opposite-direction group morphism; no surjectivity of f is assumed. Checks pass: [exteriorAlgebra_corestrict](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Corestrict.lean#L51), [exteriorAlgebraCoact_ι](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean#L82).
Equality of the resulting exterior-algebra comodule structures.
The coefficient comparison is determined on generators.

The restricted degree-n coaction after coefficient change is (id⊗f) composed with the original one. The equality follows from the exterior-algebra comparison through the split homogeneous inclusion. Thus exterior powers commute with restriction under the dictionary of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); the construction needs a bialgebra morphism, not merely an arbitrary linear map. Checks pass: [exteriorPower_corestrict](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Corestrict.lean#L86), [subtype_rTensor_exteriorPowerCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Power.lean#L62).
Equality of the full exterior-power comodule structures.
The homogeneous coaction is characterized by inclusion into the exterior algebra.

Taking an exterior power and changing coefficient bialgebra give the same comodule structure on the same module Λⁿ(M). Equality of their coactions proves this, including degree zero. It is the compatibility of exterior representations with restriction in the dictionary of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); corestriction changes coefficients, not the base ring or carrier module. Checks pass: [exteriorPowerCoact_corestrict](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Corestrict.lean#L69), [exteriorAlgebra_corestrict](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ExteriorAlgebra/Corestrict.lean#L51).
Equality of the actual coaction maps.
The ambient exterior-algebra construction has the same compatibility.

The product of two finite nonnegative extended reals is finite, including when either factor is zero. This is a sufficient condition, not an equivalence: a product can also be finite with an infinite factor, because this arithmetic defines 0·∞=0. Thus finiteness of a product alone does not force both factors finite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L204).

Multiplying a nonzero extended nonnegative real by infinity gives infinity. The nonzero assumption allows the other factor itself to be infinity, so ∞·∞=∞ is included. Zero must be excluded because Lean uses 0·∞=0, rather than leaving that product undefined or treating infinity as an ordinary real number. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L188).

Infinity multiplied by any nonzero extended nonnegative real is infinity. This includes an infinite second factor; no finiteness assumption is hidden. The excluded zero case has value zero under Lean’s convention ∞·0=0. The theorem therefore expresses multiplication by infinity only on the positive part of the domain. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L193).

Two nonzero extended nonnegative reals have a strictly positive product. Neither factor has to be finite: multiplying infinity by any positive value gives infinity, which is positive in the extended order. Nonzero and positive are equivalent here because negative values are absent; allowing a zero factor would instead give zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L228).

For extended nonnegative reals, increasing the numerator and decreasing the denominator cannot decrease the quotient: a≤b and d≤c imply a/c≤b/d. No finiteness or nonzero assumptions are needed for this weak inequality. Lean’s endpoint conventions, including 0/0=0 and every value divided by infinity being zero, are compatible with it. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L469).

An extended nonnegative quotient is infinite exactly when its numerator is nonzero and denominator zero, or its numerator is infinite and denominator finite. These alternatives may overlap at ∞/0. They deliberately exclude 0/0 and ∞/∞, both defined as zero here; ordinary division rules cannot be applied to those endpoints. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L352).

A quotient of extended nonnegative reals is zero exactly when its numerator is zero or its denominator is infinity. This includes the conventions 0/0=0 and ∞/∞=0. A positive numerator divided by zero is instead infinity, so a zero denominator by itself does not make the quotient zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L547).

A finite extended nonnegative numerator divided by a nonzero denominator has a finite quotient. The denominator may be infinity, in which case the result is zero. These hypotheses are sufficient rather than necessary: 0/0 is also zero and finite. No claim is made that a finite quotient determines either hypothesis. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L219).

The reciprocal of an extended nonnegative real is infinity exactly when the input is zero. Positive finite values have their usual finite reciprocals, while infinity has reciprocal zero. This is a deliberate extension of ordinary reciprocal: unlike Lean’s real-number reciprocal, the reciprocal of zero in this type is infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L204).

An extended nonnegative reciprocal equals zero precisely when the original value is infinity. In particular, a finite input always has a nonzero reciprocal, even at input zero, whose reciprocal is infinity. The distinction matters because ordinary real arithmetic in Lean instead defines the reciprocal of zero to be zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L222).

An extended nonnegative reciprocal is finite exactly when the input is nonzero. The input itself need not be finite: infinity is nonzero and has reciprocal zero, which is finite. Conversely, input zero produces infinity. Thus this criterion concerns finiteness of the output and should not be read as requiring positive finite input. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L206).

An extended nonnegative reciprocal is nonzero exactly when the input is finite. The input is allowed to be zero: its reciprocal is infinity, which is nonzero in this domain. Only an infinite input produces zero. Hence “nonzero reciprocal” does not guarantee that both input and output are positive and finite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L225).

A positive finite extended nonnegative real multiplied by its reciprocal equals one, just as in ordinary arithmetic. Both exclusions matter: zero and infinity exchange under reciprocal, and their product is zero because 0·∞=0. Therefore the inverse law is valid on positive finite values, not on the entire extended domain. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L104).

For a positive finite extended nonnegative value, its reciprocal multiplied by the value equals one. This is the reversed product form of the usual inverse law; multiplication here is commutative. Zero and infinity are excluded because each multiplied by its reciprocal gives zero under the convention 0·∞=0, not one. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L109).

A common positive finite factor can be cancelled from an inequality of extended nonnegative products: a·c≤b·c exactly when a≤b. The compared values a and b may be infinite. The factor restrictions are essential: multiplication by zero collapses everything, while multiplication by infinity identifies distinct positive finite values. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L80).

Multiplying both sides of an extended nonnegative comparison on the left by a positive finite value preserves and reflects the inequality: a·b≤a·c exactly when b≤c. Either compared value may be infinity. A zero or infinite common multiplier cannot be cancelled, since it can send distinct inputs to the same value. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L76).

Right multiplication by a positive finite value preserves strict inequality between extended nonnegative reals: b<c implies b·a<c·a. The larger compared value may be infinity. The multiplier must exclude both endpoints: zero collapses all products, and infinity turns the strict comparison 1<2 into equal infinite products. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L63).

Left multiplication by a positive finite value preserves strict inequality in the extended nonnegative reals: b<c implies a·b<a·c. No finiteness assumption is placed on the compared values. Allowing a zero multiplier would collapse both products to zero; allowing infinity would collapse distinct positive finite inputs to infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L59).

Adding the same finite extended nonnegative value on the right preserves and reflects equality: b+a=c+a exactly when b=c. The common summand may be zero, and either compared value may be infinity. Finiteness of the common summand matters because 1+∞ and 2+∞ are equal although 1 and 2 are distinct. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L279).

A common finite summand on the left can be cancelled from equality of extended nonnegative sums: a+b=a+c exactly when b=c. The other summands need not be finite. This is not cancellation by every extended value: infinity absorbs addition, so ∞+1=∞+2 despite the unequal finite summands. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L276).

An element is regular when its centralizer, the vectors commuting with it, has the smallest dimension among all centralizers. Here dimension is a cardinal, so infinite-dimensional Lie algebras are allowed without collapsing their dimensions to zero. In finite dimensions this is the usual minimum-dimension condition; it does not require semisimplicity or an algebraically closed field. See [Kostant–Wallach, §0.1 p.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1011.3267). Native Checks pass: [Finite-dimensional centralizer-dimension comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/AdjointAction/Regular.lean#L103), [Zero is regular exactly in the finite-dimensional abelian case](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/AdjointAction/Regular.lean#L159), [Every element of an abelian Lie algebra is regular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/AdjointAction/Regular.lean#L173).

A compact subset W={f≤c} lies in the ambient manifold’s interior. Globally, ω=dα is nondegenerate and a smooth field Z satisfies ι_Zω=α. The continuous f is smooth along f=c, where df(Z)>0 means outward crossing. In finite dimensions this is a regular boundary level. For canonical cotangent ω=−dλ, its primitive is −λ. See [Seidel, §2a p.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0704.2055). Native Checks pass: [The ambient exact form is symplectic](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Liouville/Domain.lean#L98), [The compact Riemannian codisc family with primitive −λ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Cotangent/Bundle/Domain.lean#L61).

In an abelian category, take the componentwise direct sum, pull back along the diagonal on the common right endpoint, then push out along addition on the common left endpoint. Both input sequences need only have zero composite for this construction. When both are short exact, the result is their Baer sum and represents addition in Ext¹. See [Stacks, §12.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/010I). Native Checks pass: [Exact input extensions give an exact Baer sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Ext/BaerSum.lean#L52), [The actual Baer sum represents addition of extension classes](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Ext/BaerSum.lean#L103).
